summary: Built a system-level schematic of a U-shaped notebook final-assembly line with fourteen named stations, a line-side warehouse, three animated delivery vehicles, and moving notebook workpieces. Three selectable plans change staffing, test parallelism, run-in capacity, work content, and assumed OEE. Numbered hotspots support component focus, while staged narration follows loading through shipment. Equipment and workpieces use illustrative proportions. Calculations use effective station times for bottleneck and line balance; the requested effective-time WIP estimate is distinguished from physical run-in occupancy, which can be substantially higher. This is a planning visualization and takt estimate, not a discrete-event simulation or validated throughput forecast.

prompt: Build an interactive digital twin of a notebook final-assembly line (system-level schematic): 60 m U-shaped line with 14 stations: ① bottom-cover loading ② motherboard + thermal module ③ automatic screwing (6-axis robot) ④ battery + speakers ⑤ display assembly + hinges ⑥ keyboard / touchpad + C-cover closing ⑦ automatic screwing ⑧ cosmetic AOI inspection ⑨ firmware flashing & functional test (6 parallel testers) ⑩ run-in (2 h, 240-slot rack) ⑪ shipping image & final inspection ⑫ labelling + packing ⑬ cartoning & palletising (collaborative robot) ⑭ finished goods to AGV. Materials are delivered by AGVs from the line-side warehouse. Implement three switchable plans: ① one shift, 800 units / 8 h; ② two shifts, 1,800 units / 16 h (9 parallel testers, 300 run-in slots); ③ automation upgrade (on top of ②: stations ④ ⑥ ⑫ robot-assisted, 100 % AOI, fewer operators). Animate work-pieces moving on the conveyor, numbered station hotspots tagged by automation class (robot / AOI / tester / run-in rack / AGV / manual), staged narration (loading → assembly → test & run-in → packing & shipping), and compute per plan the takt time, line-balance rate, bottleneck station, WIP, headcount, units per operator-hour and an OEE estimate.
